correctness.rationale: The difference of two independent uniform cube coordinates has exactly the product triangular density. Gram positivity localizes squared-distance maximizers at vertices; weighted positive graph edges reduce vertex gap exactly to 4h times cut weight. For deficit at most ht, the inequality deficit >= sum_i(1-z_i^2) forces uniform O(h) corner localization. In each chart z_i=s_i(1-hy_i), normalized deficit tends to 4C(s)+2sum_i y_i and density times Jacobian equals h^(2d)prod_i y_i. The Dirichlet integral equals b_+^(2d)/(4^d(2d)!), producing the asserted locally uniform spline. Its distributional (2d+1)st derivative is the exact cut atomic measure. At fixed positive h, only 2^c component-constant spins maximize, their linear deficits have coefficients 2(1+h a_i), yielding the exact endpoint constant and the discontinuity ratio 2^(c-d). The independent checker completed rational spin calculations and independent 2D quadrature with VERIFY_OK. No finite computation is used as proof of an infinite assertion.

originality.rationale: The relevant 2026 geometric-probability paper establishes a covariogram framework and Brunn-Minkowski theory, without the weighted-cut spline or singular near-diameter Gram perturbation law. A prior cube theorem concerns maximum distance over an increasing random sample, not this two-point deformation crossover. Ellipsoid maximum-distance works apply smooth-body asymptotics, not graph cut multiplicities. Relevant exact graph-cut/Ising identities are prior mathematical input; the claim is the geometric encoding and the double-limit endpoint effect. An indexed-priority search cannot preclude an older unstated equivalent derivation; residual risk is recorded.

Graph cut spectra are not complete isomorphism invariants; the theorem makes only a multiset-recovery claim.

value.rationale: The exact endpoint profile of an infinite, geometrically natural class of positively sheared parallelotopes recovers the full weighted graph-cut multiset, including repeated values and the connected-component count, through a finite-order distributional derivative. The same theorem identifies a sharp 2^(c-d) discontinuity in the highest-distance probability coefficient. These results expose a structural bridge from geometric pair-distance statistics to graph cut invariants and a nontrivial singular symmetry-breaking phenomenon. The invariant and class have direct motivation; this is not only a low-order numerical or arbitrary parameter slice.
